metadata.title: Anthropic targets doubling computing capacity to 7 gigawatts next year, NYT report

content.text:
Investing.com -- Anthropic expects to have more than 3.5 gigawatts of computing capacity by the end of this year and aims to double that figure next year, the New York Times reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the company's plans.
The projected capacity would require enough electricity to power all the homes in Chicago, underscoring the extraordinary infrastructure demands behind the artificial intelligence boom.
The expansion comes as Anthropic races to secure computing resources to support surging demand for its AI models. The company has accumulated $895.4 billion in commitments for data centers, chips and computing power through 2045, according to its updated IPO prospectus.
Nearly $70 billion of those commitments are expected to take effect over the next 12 months.
Anthropic is sourcing computing power from neocloud providers including Fluidstack, Lambda and Nscale, while also striking major agreements with technology giants. Its disclosed commitments include $121.3 billion with Google, $110 billion with Amazon, $44.9 billion with Microsoft and $120.5 billion with SpaceX.
The company is also taking a more hands-on role in infrastructure development, hiring construction and supply-chain specialists and purchasing equipment such as cooling systems for data-center projects.
The scale of the expansion highlights how access to electricity and computing infrastructure is becoming a critical competitive advantage for AI companies, while raising questions about the financial returns on increasingly expensive capacity commitments.
